test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jul 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.**
solution:
The correct answer is: **much**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, "**much**" is an appropriate word choice because it conveys the idea that despite writing two or three novels, the writer still perceives their progress as insufficient or not substantial.
 
• Using "**much**" in this context helps to emphasize the writer's feeling of dissatisfaction or disappointment in their progress.
 
• The word "much" is used to indicate a large amount or degree.
 
 
• **For example- ***After studying all night, he didn't feel much more prepared for the test.*
 
 
 
• So, it fits in the sentence grammatically and semantically.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

Complete paragraph: *I went on (1) **steadily**__** **trying to 'find out how to'; but I wrote two or three novels without feeling that I had made __(2) **much**__** **progress. It was not until I wrote 'Ethan Frome' that I suddenly felt the artisan's full (3) ______ of his implements. When 'Ethan Frome' first appeared, I was (4) ______ criticised by the reviewers for what was considered the clumsy structure of the tale. I had pondered long on this structure, had felt its peculiar difficulties, and possible awkwardness, but could think of no (5) ______ which would serve as well in the given case: and though I am far from thinking 'Ethan Frome' is my best novel, and am bored and even exasperated when I am told that it is, I am still sure that its structure is not its weak point.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The phrase "**no sooner**" is used to indicate that one action happens immediately after another action. It is not appropriate in this context.
 
• The word "**barely**" means "only just; almost not." It does not fit in the sentence grammatically or semantically.
 
• The word "**so**" is used to indicate a result or consequence. It is not appropriate in this context.
